claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with a few questions:

**First, could you please tell me the name(s) of the child or children you're applying Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm helping you assess eligibility for your son, Alex.

Before I can determine eligibility, I need to understand your specific circumstances. Let me start with some important questions:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now, to assess Alex's eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about his current situation.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me check the eligibility criteria to make sure I'm assessing this correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility rules, I can see that at 18 years old, Alex would normally only qualify for Child Benefit if he's in approved education or training. You've mentioned he's not studying at the moment.

**To help me assess this further, could you tell me: Is Alex currently employed or working?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the eligibility criteria I've reviewed, I need to clarify one more important detail:

**How many hours per week does Alex work in his full-time job?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He works about 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to make a decision about Alex's eligibility.

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, here is my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: Alex is NOT eligible for Child Benefit**

Here's why:

- Alex is 18 years old and working full-time (24 hours per week)
- He is not in approved education or training
- According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, for children aged 16 and over to qualify, they must remain in approved education or training
- Additionally, Child Benefit stops if a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training

Since Alex meets this condition (working 24+ hours per week without being in education or training), he does not qualify for Child Benefit.

If you have any other questions or if there are other children you'd like me to assess, please let me know.

Since Alex is working 24 hours per week and is not in education or training, he does not qualify for Child Benefit.
